objective: Restore installed Chromium compatibility without removing no-store, the response payload budget, cancellation, truncation detection or prior failed evidence
candidate: A native response.arrayBuffer branch only after proving the response falls within an inspected Chromium HTTP/1 framing path; every other response retains the current actual-count bounded stream path
native_conditions: Verified Chromium major 156 or158 in the observed Windows platform; other browser environments keep the current stream path
Target URL uses cleartext HTTP and the configured loopback service; HTTPS and uncertain transport keep stream path
Request origin differs from document origin and response.type is exactly cors, not basic/default/opaque
No active ServiceWorker controller before native reading; recheck after reading and abort native work if controller changes

The readable Access-Control-Expose-Headers token list explicitly contains itself, Content-Length, Content-Encoding and Transfer-Encoding; wildcard/malformed/missing declarations do not enable native mode
Content-Length is a positive safe integer within the per-endpoint success or error payload budget; invalid/malformed or over-budget lengths remain errors
Content-Encoding and Transfer-Encoding headers are genuinely absent, including absence of empty or identity-valued headers
Existing exact URL, no redirect, credentials omission, media, HTTP status and source/mask/GLB validation remain in force
native_completion: Preserve timeout and explicit abort. Require complete body byteLength equal to the declared length and within the budget before parsing or publishing. Never cancel/abort an already-complete successful body. Context changes fail closed with cleanup
bound_scope: Response payload bytes exposed to the application on the inspected/observed Chromium HTTP/1 transport. Not a universal RFC-only theorem for all UAs, not process RSS, GPU memory or internal browser/network copies
fallback: Unknown UA/version/platform, same-origin/basic/default, ServiceWorker, HTTPS, invisible framing metadata, missing length, content/transfer coding or uncertain conditions use the existing bounded stream consumer; never downgrade to an unbounded native read
counterexample_preserved: Header-only candidate failed: a ServiceWorker can synthesize type basic and a matching URL with small Content-Length while native consumption greatly exceeds budget. This candidate is not implemented or accepted
required_controls: Installed Chrome and Edge real cross-origin HTTP no-store positive split/multi-chunk responses with exact payload hashes and native network finished events
Current stream negative baseline reproduces the previously observed Chromium completion annotation defect
Over-budget declared length rejected before native body consumption; missing length/chunked and hidden or compressed encoding keep actual-count stream budget

Raw HTTP excess body data cannot reach the application beyond declared payload length; excess may be discarded or rejected according to Chromium parser behavior, not necessarily reported as a transport error
Truncation, conflicting lengths and malformed transfer framing remain failures
ServiceWorker basic/synthetic responses never select native; controller change cancels unfinished native consumption
Abort and timeout release the client waiter and body resources without changing native service lease semantics
Actual research worker/session/display run in installed Chrome and Edge, independent raw RGBA/geometry/source-age/provenance audit and owned cleanup; no route mocks or known-error whitelist
